adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — .custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30% (dark 70%), inverting the muted hint to near-body contrast and diverging from desktop/modal.scss (70%/30%).

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss, .custom-message-length changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which is an inversion relative to the pattern used elsewhere and specifically diverges from desktop/modal.scss where it is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — Light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50% (dark 50% instead of 80%), inconsistent with the desktop counterpart that keeps 20%/80%.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss within the `a.star h3` rule, the color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which does change the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50% (and uses 50% for the dark choice rather than something like 80%). In the desktop counterpart (app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss), the analogous `h3` rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, so the finding’s inconsistency claim is grounded in the diff. Whether this is a “bug” is not provable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete inconsistency introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:385 — The same `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, L), scale-color($secondary, 100-L))` expression is copied inline about 109 times across 30 files; put it in a single SCSS function or mixin so theme logic lives in one place.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many prior `scale-color($primary, ...)` uses with inline `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))` across a large number of SCSS files (e.g., admin_base.scss, topic-list.scss, header.scss, etc.), creating obvious repetition of the same pattern. While the exact “109 times across 30 files” count isn’t verifiable from the snippet alone, the duplication itself is clearly introduced by this PR and a mixin/function would centralize the theme logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss:48 — The new inline pattern ignores the existing `dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, X%, Y%)` helper, which is already used about 129 times for the same light/dark adjustment, so there are now two competing ways to do it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss (e.g. the `th`/`td`/`.topic-excerpt` color changes around lines 45-70), the diff replaces `scale-color($primary, ...)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary,...), scale-color($secondary,...))` rather than using the existing `dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, X%, Y%)` helper. The diff itself also shows `dark-light-diff` still being used in other files/areas (e.g. common/base/header.scss and desktop/topic-post.scss), so this change does introduce/expand a second pattern for handling light/dark theme adjustments, which is a maintainability/consistency concern (not a correctness defect). The specific claim that `dark-light-diff` is used "about 129 times" cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/discourse.scss:73 — The comment still says the table-cell default is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, but the code it describes now uses the dark-light-choose form.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:1 — Every call site hand-computes the complementary percentage (for example 40%/60% and 80%/20%), so each lightness level becomes two magic numbers that must be kept in sync by hand.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many single `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` usages with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: Y%))`, e.g. `desktop/topic-post.scss` and numerous other files. In many cases `Y` is manually chosen as a complementary-looking value to `X` (e.g. 40/60, 75/25, 20/80), meaning the pairing is repeated as two independent “magic numbers” at each call site rather than being derived. This is a maintainability concern introduced by the change, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.
